scope: Theorem 2.6 (Order presentation) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 11-12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Suppose K has arbitrarily large models and LS(K) = ℓ. There are at most ℓ labels, each of positive finite arity, and a functor E from nonempty linear orders and order embeddings to K and strong maps, with the following properties. 1. Every element of E(I) is a label evaluated on an increasing finite list from I. Equality and all structure relations and function values are determined by the labels and the order/equality pattern of the finitely many indices involved. 2. E(I) contains distinct distinguished elements (ai)i∈I. An order embedding f : I −→ J sends ai to af(i), and its action on any labeled element is position substitution. 11 3. For every finite nonempty s ⊆ I, the elements labeled on s form a strong submodel Es(I) of cardinality at most ℓ. For s ⊆ t these submodels are strongly included, and E(I) = S s Es(I). 4. |I| ≤ ∥E(I)∥ ≤ |I| + ℓ. In particular, for every infinite κ ≥ ℓ, K has a model of cardinality exactly κ. Here a subpresentation is identified with its image under the canonical strong map when an inclusion of underlying universes is convenient.
